themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 135 THIS WEEK—a 419% spike versus the 26-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting rapid deterioration across Sunnyside/Woodside's road network, compounded by concurrent spikes in sidewalk condition (9 complaints this week vs. 3.4 avg) and dangling street signs (7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.6 avg).
evidence: Street Condition: 135 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 26.0 weekly average (z-score: 11.01, up 419%)
Sidewalk Condition: 9 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.4 average (up 167%)
Street Sign - Dangling: 7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.6 average (up 167%)
reporting_angles: Walking tour documenting potholes, cracked sidewalks, and hazardous conditions with resident interviews about commute safety
Investigation into DOE/DSNY street maintenance schedules—has seasonal winter damage accelerated? Are repair crews falling behind?

themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Missed garbage collection complaints jumped to 16 THIS WEEK—a 540% spike from the 2.5-complaint weekly baseline over 8 weeks—indicating a significant sanitation service disruption affecting residential blocks and potentially creating health/rodent concerns.
evidence: Missed Collection: 16 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.04, up 540%)
Street Sweeping Complaint: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.2 average (up 1900%)
Cumulative sanitation pressure: 21 complaints over 2 weeks for sweeping + collection combined
reporting_angles: Call DSNY to determine cause of missed pickups—staffing shortage, route changes, weather delays, or equipment failure?
Photo/video documentation of overflowing bins and street debris; interview residents about impact on block cleanliness and pest activity

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting/Advertising Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints exploded to 5 LAST WEEK—a 3900% spike from the 0.1-complaint weekly baseline—representing an unprecedented infestation of unauthorized signage (flyers, posters, graffiti tags) across the district.
evidence: Illegal Posting: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 14.74, up 3900%)
This represents the single largest statistical anomaly in the dataset by z-score
reporting_angles: Visual documentation of hotspots—which blocks/intersections are most affected? Are postings political, commercial, or spam-related?
Interview community board or local merchants about whether this is linked to a particular event, campaign, or organized activity

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures Surge
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints jumped to 131 LAST WEEK—a 188% spike from the 45.5-complaint weekly average—raising safety concerns at intersections and potentially indicating aging infrastructure or recent weather-related damage.
evidence: Traffic Signal Condition: 131 complaints last week vs. 45.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.31, up 188%)
Traffic Signal Condition is already among top 10 complaint categories over 90 days (852 total complaints)
reporting_angles: Safety audit—visit reported signal failures during commute hours; document malfunctioning lights and near-miss incidents
Interview DOT about maintenance protocols; are signals on a replacement cycle? What's the age of the signaling infrastructure in CD 402?

themes_detail.label: Building Maintenance Issues Rising
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints spiked to 14 LAST WEEK—a 239% increase from the 4.1-complaint weekly baseline—suggesting growing problems with building systems, HVAC, or public facility upkeep across residential and commercial properties.
evidence: Maintenance or Facility: 14 complaints last week vs. 4.1 weekly average (z-score: 3.77, up 239%)
Heat/hot water remains a chronic top-10 issue (1791 complaints over 90 days), suggesting winter-season vulnerability in aging buildings
reporting_angles: Determine breakdown of complaints—are they residential buildings, schools, libraries, parks? Which agencies are most frequently cited?
Interview tenants in buildings with multiple complaints; cross-reference with HPD violations and DOB permits to identify chronic problem properties
